content_html:
An FHA loan is a home loan backed by the Federal Housing Administration, an agency within HUD, which repays the lender if the borrower defaults. They allow a down payment as low as 3.5%, but every FHA borrower pays mortgage insurance premiums (MIP): an upfront premium at closing and an annual premium paid monthly. This calculator applies HUD's current premium rules to estimate your full monthly payment and the total cost of mortgage insurance.

How to use this calculator

  1. Home price and down payment: enter the down payment as a percentage or a dollar amount. FHA requires at least 3.5% with a credit score of 580 or higher, and 10% with a score from 500 to 579.
  2. Interest rate and loan term: the rate from your lender and a term from 10 to 30 years.
  3. Upfront MIP: leave the box ticked to add it to the loan, as most borrowers do, or untick it to pay it in cash at closing.
  4. Taxes, insurance and fees: property tax, homeowners insurance and any HOA dues, to see the full monthly payment.

FHA mortgage insurance rules

The upfront premium is 1.75% of the base loan amount (the price minus your down payment). The annual premium depends on the loan term, the base loan amount and the loan-to-value ratio (LTV), under rates HUD set in Mortgagee Letter 2023-05, which still apply in 2026. The loan-size line is the national conforming loan limit, $832,750 for 2026:

TermBase loan amountLTVAnnual MIP
Over 15 years$832,750 or less95% or less / over 95%0.50% / 0.55%
Over 15 yearsOver $832,75095% or less / over 95%0.70% / 0.75%
15 years or less$832,750 or less90% or less / over 90%0.15% / 0.40%
15 years or lessOver $832,75078% or less / 78–90% / over 90%0.15% / 0.40% / 0.65%

If your LTV is 90% or less, which means a down payment of at least 10%, annual MIP stops after 11 years. Otherwise it lasts for the life of the loan, and the usual way to remove it is to refinance into a different loan. Each year HUD recalculates the premium on the average balance scheduled for that year, so it falls slowly as you pay the loan down.

Worked example

A $400,000 home with 3.5% down ($14,000) leaves a base loan of $386,000. The upfront MIP is $6,755, so the financed loan is $392,755. At 6.25% for 30 years:

Monthly costAmount
Principal and interest$2,418.26
Annual MIP (0.55%), first year$175.98
Property tax (1.1% a year)$366.67
Home insurance ($1,800 a year)$150.00
Total first-year payment$3,110.91

With 3.5% down, annual MIP runs for all 30 years, and mortgage insurance totals $48,080.12 including the upfront premium. With 10% down, the annual rate drops to 0.50% and stops after 11 years.

Before you apply

  • FHA loan limits vary by county and change every year. Look up the limit for your area with HUD's FHA mortgage limits search on hud.gov. This calculator does not check it.
  • Your lender also looks at your debt-to-income ratio and requires the home to meet FHA property standards.
  • Compare the total cost with a conventional loan. With a strong credit score and 5% to 10% down, private mortgage insurance can cost less and can be cancelled once you build enough equity.

faq.question: What credit score do I need for an FHA loan?
faq.answer: FHA rules allow a 3.5% down payment with a credit score of 580 or higher and require 10% down for scores from 500 to 579. Many lenders set their own higher minimums.

faq.question: Can I remove FHA mortgage insurance?
faq.answer: If you put at least 10% down, annual MIP ends after 11 years. With less than 10% down it lasts for the life of the loan, so the main way to remove it is to refinance into a different type of loan.

faq.question: Is the upfront MIP refundable?
faq.answer: Part of it may be credited toward a new FHA loan if you refinance into another FHA loan within three years. Otherwise it is not refunded.

faq.question: Why is my lender's MIP figure slightly different?
faq.answer: HUD bases the annual premium on the average scheduled balance for each year and rounds at several steps. Small differences in rate, loan amount or closing date can change the figure by a few dollars.

faq.question: Does the calculator check FHA loan limits?
faq.answer: No. Limits depend on your county and are updated each year, so check HUD's FHA mortgage limits search for your area before you apply.
